title: Australian Wheat Crop Rebounds at Key Time for Supply
summary: Prospects for Australia’s upcoming wheat crop are turning more optimistic, helping to buffer an increasingly grim global supply outlook for the grain.

title: Adnoc Gas Exploring New LNG Export Plant to Avoid Hormuz
summary: Adnoc Gas Plc is considering a new liquefied natural gas export facility outside the contested Strait of Hormuz, Abu Dhabi’s latest move to build infrastructure bypassing the critical waterway that’s been severely disrupted by the Iran war.

title: Indonesia Nominates Destry as Central Bank Chief to Calm Markets
summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto nominated Acting Governor Destry Damayanti as the sole candidate to head Bank Indonesia, advancing a hiring process that has attracted attention from global investors since veteran Perry Warjiyo unexpectedly resigned from the post in late July.

title: What's Next for Cockroach Janta Party After Protests
summary: Following India's student-led protests that pushed education reform into the national spotlight, Cockroach Janta Party spokesperson Ashutosh Ranka discusses the movement’s next steps, concerns over alleged harassment of protesters, and why the group is choosing to remain a pressure movement rather than enter electoral politics. He spoke to Bloomberg's Menaka Doshi on Insight with Haslinda Amin. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Egypt Headline Inflation Quickens for the First Time Since March
summary: Egypt’s inflation rate accelerated for the first time since March, disrupting an easing streak that had lasted for much of the ongoing US-Iran war.

title: Global Stock Rally Extends, Oil Pares Advance: Markets Wrap
summary: Global stocks traded near a record high as Asian shares tracked Wall Street higher after soft US jobs data eased expectations for a Federal Reserve interest-rate hike. Oil pared earlier gains as a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz remained elusive.

title: Bohl: Iran Won’t Succumb to Trump’s Pressure Campaign
summary: Iran has promoted a hardline ex-commander as its top security official, shaking up its highest decision-making body on national defense. It comes after Tehran said it was "very close" to a deal with Oman, over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz but say there has been no negotiations with the US. Ryan Bohl, Senior Middle East and North Africa Analyst at RANE spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar on the likely scenario in the impasse. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Adnoc Gas CFO Eyes LNG Export Plant on UAE East Coast
summary: Adnoc Gas reported net income for the second quarter of $665 million that beat the average analyst estimate even as the Mideast conflict disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. CFO Peter van Driel spoke to Bloomberg’s Abeer Abu Omar about the numbers. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Philippine Central Bank Keeps Rate Hike on Table Despite Weak GDP Growth
summary: The Philippine central bank is ready to tighten monetary policy further to guide inflation back to target, Governor Eli Remolona said, while adding that there’s less pressure to do so after last quarter’s surprise economic slowdown.

title: Netanyahu Rejects Hamas Disarmament Proposal
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu rejected a proposal by US-backed mediators for disarming Hamas, hardening his position after voicing misgivings at the suggestion that Israel reciprocate with phased pullouts from Gaza. Bloomberg's Dan Williams reports on Bloomberg Daybreak Europe.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: FTSE 100 Live: UK Stocks Set to Fall, Pound Steadies
Iran Shakes Up Security Team Claiming Oman Deal ‘Close’
summary: Iran promoted a hard-line ex-commander as its top security official, shaking up its highest decision-making body on national defense after saying it was “very close” to a deal with Oman over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz. Bloomberg's Stuart Livingstone-Wallace shares what we know about the situation. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: China’s Slower-Than-Expected Price Gains Revive Deflation Risk
summary: China’s consumer prices grew at the slowest pace in six months while factory-gate inflation eased for the first time since the Iran war broke out in late February, in another sign that reflation momentum is fading as the oil shock subsides and domestic spending languishes.

title: Netanyahu Rejects US-Backed Hamas Disarmament Proposal
summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected a proposal by US-backed mediators for disarming Hamas, saying "Israel does not accept the 15-point document". Bloomberg's Dan Williams breaks down the developments. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Copper Holds $14,000 as Weaker US Rate Outlook Boosts Metals
summary: Copper traded in a narrow range after six straight weeks of gains, fueled by tightening supplies and easing concerns about US interest-rate hikes.

title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Aug. 10
summary: Oil extended gains as Iran and Oman remained short of a deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, while Houthi militants claimed an attack on a Saudi refinery near the Red Sea.

title: NYSE President on Asia Business, IPO Pipeline
summary: Lynn Martin, President at the NYSE Group, discuses the exchange's business strategy and priorities in Asia, as well as the IPO pipeline in the US. She speaks with Paul Allen on Insight with Haslinda Amin.  (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Emerging-Market Stocks, Currencies Gain After Soft US Jobs Data
summary: Emerging-market stocks and currencies climbed at the start of a new week as expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes eased following Friday’s unexpectedly weak US employment report.

title: Jobs Data Won't Move Fed's Thinking: Natixis' Hodge
summary: Christopher Hodge, Natixis Chief US Economist, expects a modest uptick in unemployment in the upcoming US jobs report. He joins Bloomberg's Vonnie Quinn on "Bloomberg Brief." (Source: Bloomberg)
